clue.text: Marine store in Hong Kong?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a dealer in old ships' gear and second-hand naval supplies
setter's reading: a shop aboard one of the flat-bottomed Chinese sailing boats seen in Hong Kong harbour

explanation.walkthrough: A marine store was the old name for a dealer in second-hand ships' goods; the question mark invites you to read the first word as a Chinese sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer selling old rope, chandlery and cast-off goods was called a marine store, the same trade as this kind of second-hand shop.

clue.text: Flier without a single chart

indicators.note: without means going short of something, so a letter is taken out of the flier

explanation.surface: A navigator in the cockpit flying blind with no map to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot a course is to mark it out on a map, so as verbs the two mean the same mapping task.

clue.text: We maintain a craftsman

parts.note: to maintain a claim is to assert it firmly

explanation.surface: A group of people declaring that they count as skilled artisans.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes cloth on a loom is a traditional skilled tradesman, an example of the broader class.

clue.text: Sport enclosure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Olympic discipline of swordplay with foil, épée or sabre
second meaning: a barrier of posts and rails around a field

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a sports ground; they are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the swordsman's competitive pursuit and the posts and wire that surround a paddock or garden.

clue.text: The mark of a finished writer?

definitions.text: The mark of a finished writer?

parts.words: The mark of a finished writer?
parts.note: surface reading: the sign of an accomplished, polished author; setter's reading: the punctuation dot placed when someone writing has come to the end of a sentence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished' looks like praise for a writer's skill but means simply having stopped writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot ending a sentence is the punctuation mark put down when a writer has come to a halt.

clue.text: Charmian so upset — a drink is needed

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Charmian, Cleopatra's attendant, is distressed and needs something stiff to steady her nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sweet cherry liqueur from Dalmatia, so a drink of the alcoholic kind.

clue.text: Hide or show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shield something from view
second meaning: to project a film for an audience

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are near opposites, which is the joke: one word both conceals and displays.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means both conceal behind a partition and broadcast a film or programme to viewers.

clue.text: Sweet dog Bill Sikes owned

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hard, striped peppermint boiled sweet
second meaning: the bull terrier belonging to the burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal housebreaker in Oliver Twist; 'Sweet dog' looks like an affectionate phrase about his pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a round striped mint candy and the savage pet terrier of Dickens's villain.

clue.text: Period for redemption, states article by church

explanation.surface: A churchman setting out how long the American states allow a sinner to win salvation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds religious, redemption of souls, but redemption here is paying off a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce this is the customary time allowed for paying a foreign bill of exchange, the term before it must be honoured.

clue.text: Take off in second gear

explanation.surface: A car pulling away from the lights with the gearbox in second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' is a noun here, a parody, not a verb about departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a comic imitation, and a short comic sketch parodying someone is the same thing.

clue.text: Was irresolute, being abandoned and sick at heart

indicators.note: at heart places one word in the middle of another, so sick sits inside abandoned

explanation.surface: Someone left behind and heartsick, unable to make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver back and forth without deciding is exactly to be irresolute, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Rabble's downfall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a hopeless, disorderly group of people
second meaning: a fall of rain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the overthrow of a mob; in Britain calling a group 'a right shower' means they are useless, and downfall is literal falling rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a contemptible bunch in British slang and a brief burst of rain coming down.

clue.text: Warn omelet is off, but may still be eaten

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the noun: the fruit that can still be eaten

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A waiter cautions that the omelette has gone off, though something else on the menu is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a food that remains edible even when the omelette is off the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A large juicy fruit is something one can still eat, so it fits the loosely phrased description of an edible item.

clue.text: Recognising gin and tonic ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are things mixed together, so the letters of the two words are blended

explanation.surface: A drinker identifying what has gone into a classic gin and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting or becoming aware of something is to recognise it, both present participles.

clue.text: It's usually written to one unable to read it

definitions.text: It's usually written to one unable to read it

parts.words: It's usually written to one unable to read it
parts.note: surface reading: a letter addressed to a blind or illiterate person; setter's reading: the dead person in the grave, who cannot read the words carved above

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a letter to someone who cannot read; the reader who cannot read is in fact dead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the inscription on a tombstone commemorating someone deceased, who of course cannot read it.

clue.text: Fair examinations should be!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: adequate, tolerably good

definitions.note: a predicate: what examinations should be
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: capable of being passed

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a demand that exams be fair; the second sense splits the word as able to be passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merely adequate is described as fair or tolerable; and any test ought to be one candidates are able to pass.

clue.text: Joined by a sailor — or a parson

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rope ends united by a seaman interweaving their strands

definitions.note: read with the opening words: joined by a parson
definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for a couple who have been married by the clergyman

explanation.walkthrough: Seamen join ropes by interweaving strands; informally a married couple are said to have been joined the same way by the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rope ends woven together and, colloquially, a couple wed by a clergyman.

clue.text: Growth of conciliation overturned by workers — a bad sign

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the word backwards

parts.note: the olive branch is the traditional token of peace

explanation.surface: A peace offering trampled by striking workers bodes ill for negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent of trouble to come is a bad sign, the same idea in plainer words.

clue.text: How schoolboys are punished and journalists recognised?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: ..., the British school penalty of copying out a sentence many times
second meaning: the printed lines crediting a reporter with an article

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools 'lines' is a punishment of writing a sentence out repeatedly; the 'How' serves both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers credit a reporter's work with a printed author line, the way a journalist's name is acknowledged in print.

clue.text: Island off the Needles?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the Channel Islands
second meaning: a thick knitted sailor's jumper, just taken off the knitting needles

explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, so 'Island off the Needles' sounds geographical; the second sense is knitting, and the jumper takes its name from the island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Channel Island and also a close-knit woollen sweater worn by fishermen, freshly finished by the knitter.

clue.text: Rough? That's odd

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bumpy, not smooth
second meaning: of a number not divisible by two

explanation.walkthrough: 'That's odd' reads as surprise; odd is the number sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpy irregular surface is not level, and numbers like three or seven cannot be halved into whole parts.

clue.text: Informally visit doctor at home about a small operation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the doctor and home together wrap round the operation

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A GP calls at a patient's house to carry out a minor procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone casually without arranging it is a phrasal verb for paying an informal visit.

clue.text: Complete exposure of corruption in Dundee

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a verb: to expose completely

indicators.note: corruption is spoiling or perverting, so the city's letters are spoilt into another order

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposé uncovering graft in the Scottish city of Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip something bare is to lay it fully open, so it means exposing totally.

clue.text: Flora vetoing tea break

indicators.note: to break is to smash into bits, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A woman named Flora refusing to allow anyone a tea break at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant life of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: The plants of an area taken collectively are its plant life, the botanical term matching the growth covering land.

clue.text: When corruption is about, I show no respect for authority

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so the decay wraps around the single letter

explanation.surface: A protester explaining that rampant graft is why they defy the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: The I does double duty in the surface as speaker, but in the wordplay it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a violent public disturbance is the extreme way of defying law and order.

clue.text: Small pig has nose tip embedded in furrow

indicators.note: embedded in means set inside, so one piece goes within the furrow
a tip is the very end, here the front point of the word nose

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A little piglet rooting about with its snout buried in a ploughed groove.
explanation.definitionFit: The weakest and smallest animal in a litter, especially of piglets, is called this.

clue.text: Spring back after being fired

definitions.meaning: surface reading: bounce back after losing a job
setter's reading: what a gun does when it is discharged, kicking back against the shoulder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests dismissal and a comeback; it means a gun being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun jerks backwards when shot, and the word also means to jump back or flinch.

clue.text: Peace-making counsel is put at risk

wordplay.note: advice to a quarrelling party, split as two words: stop your rage

explanation.surface: A mediator's advice to warring parties turns out to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is a peacemaker's instruction to end anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose someone or something to danger or harm is to imperil it, the same verb meaning.
